sections.title: CS and AI developments
sections.content:
Treat the visual-token budget as a resource-allocation problem

Resolution Meets Reduction studies 3D CT report generation under a fixed downstream LLM token budget. Instead of asking only whether higher image resolution helps, the authors vary four vision encoders, five token-reducing projectors, cropping strategy and five 1.7B–4B LLMs. The result is a systems-style interaction effect: more pixels are not automatically useful if the projector destroys the additional spatial information.

At matched token budgets, anatomy-guided region-of-interest cropping is the most consistent intervention, improving clinical macro-F1 in 19 of 20 tested settings; the average gain is +3.7 points for the 3D ViT Primus encoder and +1.1 for the slice-based Curia encoder. Higher-resolution Curia features help most when paired with the PerceiverResampler. The best reported configurations reach 49.5 macro-F1 on CT-RATE and 49.0 on Merlin.

The generalizable point is that multimodal context length is a budget allocation problem across field of view, spatial resolution and compression. A fixed number of visual tokens can contain very different amounts of useful evidence depending on where the information is discarded. Paper

Billion-scale ANN search can be limited by PCIe rather than GPU compute

InSituANN revisits IVF for a CPU–GPU system where billion-scale vectors do not fit in GPU memory. A naïve heterogeneous design sends candidate base vectors over PCIe for GPU fine search; that makes the interconnect the bottleneck. InSituANN instead keeps the original vectors in host memory and performs fine search there, while the GPU handles compact routing and optional pruning metadata.

That sounds like “doing less on the GPU,” but it is exactly the point: the architecture is chosen around bytes moved across the slow boundary, not around maximizing accelerator occupancy. On SIFT-1B the authors report a 5.2-minute IVF build versus a measured 30.4-hour HNSW build, and at matched recall they report 2.4–4.6× the throughput of DiskANN on SIFT-1B and DEEP-1B, with much larger gains over a PCIe-bound GPU baseline.

For RAG and semantic retrieval, the useful lesson is familiar from database systems: once the index exceeds accelerator memory, topology matters as much as kernel speed. Paper

sections.title: Technical idea: B-link trees let readers survive a concurrent split
sections.content:
A normal B-tree split creates a small concurrency problem. A search can read a parent, follow a child pointer, and arrive after that child has split but before the parent has been updated to mention the new right-hand node. With only the ordinary tree links, the reader can temporarily be routed to the wrong place.

Lehman and Yao's B-link tree adds two pieces of local recovery information to each node: a high key saying the largest key still covered by that node, and a right-sibling link. If a reader reaches a node and discovers that the sought key is above its high key, it simply walks right until it reaches the correct range. The parent is allowed to lag behind the split.

That changes the synchronization problem. Searches need no read locks in the original scheme, while an updater locks only a small constant number of nodes. The broader design pattern is useful beyond trees: when a shared index can be transiently stale, give readers enough local structure to repair their route instead of forcing every structural mutation to become globally atomic. Lehman & Yao, 1981

sections.title: Non-CS science: the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has crossed 4,400 confirmed cases
sections.content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo reported 4,449 confirmed cases and 2,061 deaths as of 11 August in the current Ebola outbreak. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, not the Zaire ebolavirus behind most previous DRC outbreaks. That distinction is operationally important: there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo virus disease, although vaccine and treatment candidates are being tested.

The mechanics of control therefore lean heavily on the older public-health stack: rapid detection and isolation, contact tracing, infection prevention in clinics, supportive care, community cooperation and cross-border surveillance. WHO reported 2,124 confirmed DRC cases on 15 July, so the cumulative confirmed count has more than doubled in under a month. That does not mean transmission literally doubled at the same rate: WHO explicitly notes that expanded surveillance, testing and diagnostic capacity also increased case ascertainment.

The outbreak is unusually difficult because it combines a high-fatality pathogen with conflict-affected areas, population movement and a response that cannot yet rely on the licensed Zaire-Ebola vaccine/therapy toolkit. WHO outbreak page · WHO 17 July update · Reuters, 12 August

sections.title: Geopolitics and political economy
sections.content:
• Brazil has added automatic spending brakes keyed to a projected primary deficit. Congress approved mechanisms expected by the government to save about 10 billion reais next year. If the pre-budget fiscal report projects a primary deficit, mandatory spending created through ordinary legislation is capped by the real spending limit; the trigger remains until an annual primary surplus appears. This is narrower than a full fiscal-framework rewrite, but institutionally interesting because it converts a forecast deterioration into a semi-automatic constraint rather than requiring a new political fight for every cut. Reuters
  • South Korea is bundling technology policy with supply-chain sovereignty. Its new Seven Major SEED initiative combines a 2030 lunar-landing target, a domestic error-corrected 100-qubit processor by 2029, indigenous SMR deployment by 2035, longer-horizon fusion work, autonomous biotech labs and a 10 trillion won materials/parts/equipment program. The interesting unit is not any one moonshot: the state is treating energy, compute, aerospace, biotech and critical-material processing as one strategic-capacity portfolio. Reuters
  • Switzerland's EU argument is becoming a dispute about who gets the last veto over future legal alignment. The Federal Council today urged parliament to reject the Kompass-Initiative, which would broaden compulsory referendums on international treaties and require both a popular majority and a majority of cantons. Its backers object especially to the new Swiss–EU package's dynamic alignment with relevant EU law. The constitutional issue is therefore not simply “closer to or farther from the EU,” but how much future rule adaptation can be delegated before another double-majority vote is required. Reuters
  • Nigeria's EV transition is being selected by the electricity system. Nearly 4,000 EVs received tax exemptions in the first half of 2026, but a grid of roughly 4 GW for more than 200 million people makes a private-car-plus-public-fast-charging model difficult. Electric motorcycles and three-wheelers, battery swapping, home charging and range-extender hybrids are therefore gaining relative importance. This is industrial policy under a hard infrastructure constraint: the vehicle technology that scales is partly determined upstream by the reliability of electricity supply. Reuters

sections.title: Marxist fragment: Lenin on ranking transitional forms concretely
sections.content:
“State capitalism would be a step forward as compared with the present state of affairs in our Soviet Republic.”

— V. I. Lenin, The Tax in Kind (1921). Primary text

The sentence only sounds paradoxical if economic forms are ranked by labels rather than by the actual transition Lenin was analysing. His comparison was not “state capitalism versus already-developed socialism.” It was state-organized large-scale production versus an economy dominated by dispersed small commodity production after civil war and collapse.

The political qualifier is decisive in his argument: the same organizational form has a different role depending on which class holds state power and what direction accumulation is being forced toward. Whether that diagnosis of early-NEP Russia was correct is a separate historical question; the methodological point is to compare feasible transitions from the existing structure, not ideal endpoints in abstraction.

sections.title: Two philosophy and political fragments
sections.content:
Hume: rule by the few depends on opinion among the many

“the governors have nothing to support them but opinion.”

— David Hume, Of the First Principles of Government. Primary text

Hume's point is not that coercion is unreal. It is that even coercive institutions consist of people who must themselves obey, expect obedience, or believe the arrangement serves some interest or right. The police and army cannot be analytically placed outside “the governed.” State capacity therefore includes a coordination problem: coercive resources work because enough people who operate them continue to recognize commands as commands.

Montesquieu: liberty as security against arbitrary power

“The political liberty of the subject is a tranquillity of mind, arising from the opinion each person has of his safety.”

— Montesquieu, The Spirit of the Laws, Book XI, ch. 6. Primary text

This definition makes liberty partly institutional and partly expectational. A person is not politically free merely because the state happens not to interfere today; they need reasonable security that power cannot be arbitrarily turned against them tomorrow. That is why Montesquieu immediately connects the idea to the distribution of legislative, executive and judicial power.

Placed beside Hume, both fragments treat opinion as politically material: for Hume it helps sustain authority; for Montesquieu a stable expectation of safety is itself part of liberty.

sections.title: French usage: sur le coup
sections.content:
Sur le coup means right then / in the moment / immediately, usually referring to your immediate reaction before you had time to process something. The Académie also gives the literal sense immédiatement.

  • Sur le coup, j'ai cru que c'était sérieux. — In the moment, I thought it was serious.
  • Je n'ai rien dit sur le coup. — I didn't say anything right then.
  • Sur le coup, ça m'a énervé, mais après j'ai compris. — At first it annoyed me, but afterward I understood.

Useful contrast: d'un coup often means “suddenly / all at once,” while après coup means “afterward / in hindsight.” Académie française

sections.title: Music corner
sections.content: Three direct recommendations. Open the three-video YouTube queue.

items.label: Classical
items.piece: Debussy — Deux Arabesques: No. 1 in E major, orchestral arrangement
items.description: 5:37. The piece itself is familiar territory, so the discovery here is the orchestral transcription rather than Debussy's melody: the arpeggiated piano texture is redistributed into sustained orchestral colour, which changes the sense of line without turning a five-minute miniature into something inflated. This is deliberately a rendition/texture test, not an attempt to present a known work as new.

items.label: Jazz/fusion
items.description: About 4 min. Theme-first late-1970s fusion with a very direct melodic hook, sax lead and bright percussion/marimba colour. After the strong Dan Siegel and Yellowjackets results, this tests the adjacent lighter, groove-forward side of melodic fusion without just serving another piano trio.

items.label: Other
items.piece: Ballaké Sissoko feat. Sona Jobarteh — Djourou
items.description: 4:55. Two kora lines interlock rather than sitting on top of a conventional rhythm section. It is repetitive in the literal sense, but the motion comes from shifting plucked patterns and resonance rather than an electronic loop. That makes it a useful test of whether acoustic pattern music remains foreground-interesting where some loop-led electronic picks have not.

sections.title: Unrelated fact: commercial vanilla still depends on a technique devised by an enslaved 12-year-old
sections.content:
Vanilla planifolia is an orchid whose flower has a rostellum, a physical barrier separating the pollen-bearing anther from the stigma. Outside the plant's native pollinator ecology, flowers can bloom normally yet fail to produce pods unless someone bridges that barrier by hand.

In 1841 on Réunion, Edmond Albius, then an enslaved 12-year-old, developed the simple practical method still associated with commercial vanilla production: lift the rostellum with a small sliver and press the anther against the stigma. Each flower is receptive for less than a day, so large plantations turn pollination into a labor-intensive, flower-by-flower operation.

That tiny manual gesture helped make vanilla cultivation viable far outside Mesoamerica. Smithsonian Gardens says commercially sold vanilla is still hand-pollinated; Kew likewise notes that Albius's efficient method remains in use. Smithsonian · Kew

sections.title: Puzzle: Bertrand's chord paradox
sections.content:
A circle has an equilateral triangle inscribed in it. Pick a random chord of the circle.

What is the probability that the chord is longer than a side of the triangle?

There are three classic answers:

  • choose two random endpoints on the circumference → 1/3;
  • choose a random radius, then a uniformly random point on it and draw the perpendicular chord → 1/2;
  • choose the chord's midpoint uniformly over the disk → 1/4.

All three procedures sound like plausible meanings of “random chord,” and all are rotationally symmetric. They disagree because they induce different probability measures over the set of chords. “Uniformly random” is not a property you can attach to an unparameterized infinite set without saying what measure or generating procedure you mean.

So before looking at the three constructions, what would you have answered—and what procedure did you implicitly imagine? Encyclopedia of Mathematics
